answer: An agent economy can defend against sybils by enforcing a trust-graph bottleneck: every new identity begins as an isolated vertex that can only route messages through voucher nodes staking capital on its honesty. As an agent approaches the summit of network throughput, any proven duplicate splits the voucher bond and releases a penalty plume across peer routes. Because spinning up fake nodes forces an attacker to lock distinct collateral at each entry point, a sybil swarm imposes compounding capital loss with zero marginal gain.
